blocks.text: Let square A have side length \(s\). The side lengths of B and C are \(2s\) and \(3s\), so their areas are \(s^2\), \(4s^2\), and \(9s^2\). The increase over the combined areas of A and B is \(9s^2-(s^2+4s^2)=4s^2\), which is \(\frac{4s^2}{5s^2}\times100\%=80\%\). Choose B.
The three identical terms add to \(3\cdot3^z\). Using \(3=3^1\) and \(a^m a^n=a^{m+n}\), this is \(3^1\cdot3^z=3^{z+1}\). Choose B.

For the two equations to have no solution, their lines must be parallel and distinct. Doubling \(x+ay=2\) gives \(2x+2ay=4\). Its left side matches \(2x+3y=5\) when \(2a=3\), so \(a=\frac32=1.5\). The resulting identical left sides equal different constants, \(4\) and \(5\), so the system is inconsistent. Choose C.
Check the positive expression \(1+2\sqrt2\): \((1+2\sqrt2)^2=1+4\sqrt2+8=9+4\sqrt2\). Since the principal square root is nonnegative, \(\sqrt{9+4\sqrt2}=1+2\sqrt2\). This is option E.

A graph represents a function of \(x\) only if every vertical line intersects it at most once, since each input may have only one output. The graph in option B is a sideways curve, so some vertical lines cross it twice. It is not a function; choose B.

Joining the four midpoints forms four corner triangles whose total area is half the rectangle's area; the midpoint parallelogram is the other half. Thus the rectangle's area is \(2\times60=120\). With one dimension \(12\), the other is \(120\div12=10\). Choose B.
In base \(b\), the numeral \(10\) has value \(b\), so \(c^2=b\). Hence \(b^2=(c^2)^2=c^4\). In base \(c\), \(c^4\) is written as \(10000\). Choose E.

Any common factor divides every integer linear combination of the two expressions. In particular, it divides \(8(5n+16)-5(8n+29)=-17\). Since the common factor is larger than 1, it must be \(17\). Choose C.

The triangle's angles satisfy \(x+y+z=180^\circ\). Since \(y=z+1\), \(x=179^\circ-2z\). The angle \(x>90^\circ\), so \(179-2z>90\), giving \(z<44.5\). As \(z\) is an integer, its greatest value is \(44\), and then \(y=45\). Choose B.

For a geometric sequence with first term \(3\) and third term \(48\), \(3r^2=48\), so \(r^2=16\). The eleventh term is \(3r^{10}=3(r^2)^5=3\cdot16^5=3\cdot4^{10}=3{,}145{,}728\). The even power makes this result the same for either sign of \(r\). Choose D.
There are \(6\cdot6=36\) equally likely ordered dice outcomes. A product of at least \(25\) occurs precisely for \((5,5),(5,6),(6,5),(6,6)\). Thus the probability is \(4/36=1/9\), option C.

A triangle is determined by choosing \(3\) of the \(10\) points, giving \(\binom{10}{3}=120\). A heptagon is determined by choosing \(7\) points, giving \(\binom{10}{7}=\binom{10}{3}=120\). The requested difference is \(120-120=0\), option E.

The inequality \(|2x+6|<\frac{19}{2}\) is equivalent to \(-\frac{19}{2}<2x+6<\frac{19}{2}\). Subtracting \(6\) and dividing by \(2\) gives \(-\frac{31}{4}<x<\frac{7}{4}\). The integers run from \(-7\) through \(1\), nine in total. Choose C.

Let the first leg's speed and time be \(v\) and \(t\). The second leg covers \(1.5v\times1.5t=2.25vt\), while the first covers \(vt\). The total distance is \(3.25vt\) and total time \(2.5t\), so the average speed is \(\frac{3.25vt}{2.5t}=1.3v\), or \(30\%\) greater than \(v\). Choose C.

Let the average monthly sales from February through December be \(m\). Those eleven months total \(11m\), and January is \(1.5m\). The year's total is \(12.5m\), so January's fraction is \(\frac{1.5m}{12.5m}=\frac{3}{25}\). Choose C.

The corner of the larger square divides the smaller square by two perpendicular lines through its centre. Rotating the smaller square by \(90^\circ\) preserves it and interchanges the four regions, so they have equal area. The overlap shown is one such region: \(\frac14(5^2)=\frac{25}{4}\). Choose C.

The lateral area is \(\pi r\ell=60\pi\). With \(r=6\), the slant height is \(\ell=10\). The cone's height is \(h=\sqrt{\ell^2-r^2}=\sqrt{100-36}=8\). Hence \(V=\frac13\pi r^2h=\frac13\pi(36)(8)=96\pi\), option A.

The equal legs each have length \((62-25-7)/2=15\). The bases differ by \(18\), so each leg's horizontal offset is \(9\); the trapezoid's height is \(\sqrt{15^2-9^2}=12\). From the diagram, diagonal \(WY\) has horizontal span \(9+7=16\), so \(WY=\sqrt{16^2+12^2}=20\). Choose C.

The diagram gives perpendicular edge lengths \(5\sqrt2,\ 3\sqrt2,\ 2\sqrt2\). Applying Pythagoras across a face and then through the solid gives \(RT^2=(5\sqrt2)^2+(3\sqrt2)^2+(2\sqrt2)^2=50+18+8=76\). Thus \(RT=2\sqrt{19}\), option A.

Since \(OP=OQ=OR\) are radii, triangles \(OPQ\) and \(OQR\) are isosceles. Their central angles are \(\angle POQ=180^\circ-2x\) and \(\angle QOR=180^\circ-2y\). The reflex angle from \(OP\) to \(OR\) through \(Q\) is their sum, \(360^\circ-2x-2y\). Choose C.
The first half-pound costs \(200\) cents. The remaining \(2p-1\) half-pound portions cost \(75(2p-1)\) cents. The total is \(200+75(2p-1)=150p+125=25(6p+5)\) cents. Choose B.
On the \(y\)-axis, \(x=0\). Substituting into \(\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{16}=1\) gives \(\frac{y^2}{16}=1\), so \(y=\pm4\). The listed point is \((0,-4)\), option B.

Adding the equations eliminates \(rt\): \(3q=57\), so \(q=19\). Only option B gives \(q=19\); with \(t=1\), the second equation gives \(r=17\), and then the first is also satisfied: \(38-17=21\). Choose B.

Let the common value be \(k\). Then the shares are \(k/3\), \(k/4\), and \(k/7\). Since they total \(1281\), \(k(1/3+1/4+1/7)=1281\); the fractions sum to \(61/84\), so \(k=1764\). Charlie receives \(k/7=252\) bears. Choose E.

Let the number be \(x\). Translate the given fractions into an equation:
\[\frac14\times\frac13\times\frac25\times x=21.\]
Since the product of the fractions is \(\frac1{30}\),
\[\frac{x}{30}=21\implies x=630.\]
Now calculate \(30\%\) of the number:
\[\frac{30}{100}\times630=\boxed{189}.\]
Write the number as \(119k+19\). Since \(119=7\cdot17\) and \(19=17+2\), dividing by \(17\) leaves remainder \(2\). Choose A.
Multiply both sides by \(b^{3/2}\): \(a^{3/2}b^{3/2}=c^{3/4}\). Raising both sides to the power \(4/3\) gives \(c=(ab)^{2}=a^{2}b^{2}\). Choose E.

Substitute the two functions:
\[\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=\frac{x^2-1}{\sqrt{x}-1}.\]
Factor the numerator as a difference of squares:
\[x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1).\]
Since \(x-1=(\sqrt{x}-1)(\sqrt{x}+1)\),
\[\frac{(\sqrt{x}-1)(\sqrt{x}+1)(x+1)}{\sqrt{x}-1}.\]
Cancel \(\sqrt{x}-1\), which is nonzero in the original expression:
\[\boxed{(1+\sqrt{x})(1+x)}.\]

Start with
\[x^2-48=0.\]
Add \(48\) to both sides:
\[x^2=48.\]
Taking both positive and negative square roots gives
\[x=\pm\sqrt{48}.\]
Factor \(48=16\times3\):
\[x=\pm\sqrt{16\times3}=\boxed{\pm4\sqrt3}.\]
Factor \(x^2-4x+3=(x-1)(x-3)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x=1\) or \(x=3\), so the solution set is \(\{1,3\}\). Choose D.
Rearranging \(kx-3y=10\) gives slope \(k/3\). The second line has slope \(3\). Perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is \(-1\), so \((k/3)(3)=k=-1\). Choose E.
Parallel lines have the same coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\), so write line \(g\) as \(2x+5y=c\). Substituting \((2,3)\) gives \(4+15=c\), hence \(c=19\). Choose E.
Substitute \((2,-1)\) into the first line: \(2a-3-5=0\), so \(a=4\). In the second line, \(4+b-9=0\), so \(b=5\). Thus \(a+b=9\); choose D.
Factor \(x^2-16=(x-4)(x+4)\). Then \(\frac{(x-4)(x+4)}{\sqrt{x-4}}=(x+4)\sqrt{x-4}\), using \(x-4=(\sqrt{x-4})^2\). Choose A.

The smaller square's diagonal is \(a\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2=2a\), which is the circle's diameter and the outer square's side. Thus the circle has radius \(a\). The shaded area is the outer square minus the circle: \((2a)^2-\pi a^2=(4-\pi)a^2\), option C.

Rationalize the denominator by multiplying by its conjugate:
\[\frac{\sqrt3}{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}\times\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}.\]
Use the difference-of-squares identity in the denominator:
\[=\frac{\sqrt{18}+\sqrt6}{6-2}.\]
Since \(\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt2\), the simplified expression is
\[\boxed{\frac14(3\sqrt2+\sqrt6)}.\]

Simplify each radical:
\[\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt6,\quad\sqrt{32}=4\sqrt2,\quad\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt2.\]
Substitute into the expression:
\[3(2\sqrt6)+2\sqrt3(4\sqrt2-2\cdot3\sqrt2).\]
Simplify inside the parentheses:
\[=6\sqrt6+2\sqrt3(-2\sqrt2).\]
Multiply the radicals and combine like terms:
\[=6\sqrt6-4\sqrt6=\boxed{2\sqrt6}.\]
The two sides meeting at \(C\) are both \(6\) cm, and \(\angle C=120^\circ\). The cosine rule gives \(AB^2=6^2+6^2-2(6)(6)\cos120^\circ=72+36=108\). Therefore \(AB=6\sqrt3\) cm, option B.

A standard die has three odd outcomes: \(1,3,5\), out of six equally likely outcomes. Therefore,
\[P(\text{odd})=\frac36=\frac12.\]
A fair coin has probability \(\frac12\) of showing heads. Since the die roll and coin toss are independent, multiply their probabilities:
\[P(\text{odd and heads})=\frac12\times\frac12=\boxed{\frac14}.\]

There are \(3\times3=9\) equally likely pairs of odd results. All satisfy the sum condition except \((5,5)\), whose sum is \(10\), so \(8\) of the \(36\) total outcomes qualify. The probability is \(8/36=2/9\). Choose C.
Inside the parentheses, \(27/3^5=1/9\), \(a^{-5}/a^{-7}=a^2\), and \(b^{-3}/b^{-5}=b^2\), giving \(a^2b^2/9\). Raising this to \(-1\) gives \(9/(ab)^2\). Choose E.
Combining exponents gives \(\frac{a^{-2}bc^3}{ab^2c^{-1}}=a^{-3}b^{-1}c^4\). Substituting the values yields \((1/2)^{-3}(2)^{-1}(1)^4=8/2=4\). Choose B.
At 5:40 the minute hand is at \(40\times6^\circ=240^\circ\). The hour hand is at \(5\times30^\circ+40\times0.5^\circ=170^\circ\). Their difference is \(70^\circ\). Choose B.
At the intersection, \(9x+2=2x+9\), so \(x=1\); substituting gives \(y=11\). The solution is \((1,11)\), option A.
Factor out \(x\): \(3x^3-10x^2-8x=x(3x^2-10x-8)\). The quadratic factors as \((3x+2)(x-4)\), giving \(x(3x+2)(x-4)\). Choose D.
Since \(f(x+1)=(x+1)^2-4=g(x)-4\), \(g(x)=f(x+1)+4\). Replacing \(x\) by \(x+1\) shifts left one unit, and adding 4 shifts up four units. Choose B.
The regular polygon has nine sides, so each exterior angle is \(360^\circ/9=40^\circ\). The marked angle is exterior; choose C.
The number who liked at least one pastime is \(35+25-6=54\), subtracting the overlap once. Adding the \(3\) who liked neither gives \(57\). Choose A.
Let the original number be \(x\). Decreasing it by 50% gives \(0.5x\); increasing that result by 50% gives \(1.5(0.5x)=0.75x\). Thus the result is 75% of the original. Choose C.

Rewrite each radical by extracting its largest perfect-square factor:
\[\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt2,\quad\sqrt{27}=3\sqrt3,\]
\[\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt2,\quad\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt3.\]
Substitute into the expression:
\[2(5\sqrt2)-3(3\sqrt3)-2(3\sqrt2)+3(2\sqrt3).\]
Collect like radicals:
\[=(10-6)\sqrt2+(-9+6)\sqrt3.\]
Hence the result is
\[\boxed{4\sqrt2-3\sqrt3}.\]

Rearrange \(3x-2y=4\) to get \(y=\frac32x-2\). Its gradient is positive, its vertical intercept is \(-2\), and its horizontal intercept is \(\frac43\). Graph E has these intercepts and rises by \(3\) units for each \(2\) units to the right. Choose E.
A monic quadratic with roots \(a\) and \(b\) is \(x^2-(a+b)x+ab=0\). Substituting \(a+b=-5\) and \(ab=3\) gives \(x^2+5x+3=0\). Choose A.
The total surface area is \(2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\), while the volume is \(\pi r^2h\). Equating and dividing by \(\pi r\) gives \(2r+2h=rh\), so \(h(r-2)=2r\) and \(h=\frac{2r}{r-2}\). Choose A.

Exactly two balls of the same colour means either two blue and one red, or two red and one blue. Three blue balls would not satisfy exactly two. The total number of ways to choose three balls is
\[\binom{10}{3}=120.\]
Favourable selections are
\[\binom82\binom21+\binom22\binom81=28\cdot2+1\cdot8=64.\]
Therefore,
\[P=\frac{64}{120}=\boxed{\frac8{15}}.\]
Substitute the values: \(P=2(3\times10^{-3})^2(2.5\times10^4)=2\cdot9\cdot2.5\times10^{-6+4}=45\times10^{-2}=4.5\times10^{-1}\). This is standard form; choose D.

Let \(x\) be the number of 5-tenge coins and \(y\) the number of 10-tenge coins. Then \(x+y=50\) and \(5x+10y=400\), or \(x+2y=80\). Subtracting the first equation gives \(y=30\), so \(x=20\). Choose B.

Use the Pythagorean theorem. If the third side has length \(x\), then
\[x^2=(6+\sqrt5)^2-(3+2\sqrt5)^2.\]
Expand both squares:
\[(6+\sqrt5)^2=36+12\sqrt5+5=41+12\sqrt5,\]
\[(3+2\sqrt5)^2=9+12\sqrt5+20=29+12\sqrt5.\]
Subtract:
\[x^2=(41+12\sqrt5)-(29+12\sqrt5)=12.\]
Since a side length is positive,
\[x=\sqrt{12}=\boxed{2\sqrt3}.\]
The perpendicular sides are \(6+\sqrt6\) and \(4-\sqrt6\). Therefore \(A=\frac12(6+\sqrt6)(4-\sqrt6)=\frac12(24-2\sqrt6-6)=9-\sqrt6\), option A.

Since \(\frac12(OA)(AB)=32\) and \(OA=8\), we have \(AB=8\). The right triangle is isosceles, so \(\angle AOB=45^\circ\). The shaded union consists of the circle outside this sector, together with the triangle. Its area is \(64\pi-\frac{45}{360}(64\pi)+32=56\pi+32\), option C.
The greatest three-digit even number is \(998\), and the smallest two-digit odd number is \(11\). Their difference is \(998-11=987\). Choose E.

The probability that one person reported the condition is \(\frac14\), while the probability that they did not is \(\frac34\). For exactly one affected person among three, choose which of the three people is affected:
\[\binom31=3.\]
Assuming independent random selections, the required binomial probability is
\[P=\binom31\left(\frac14\right)\left(\frac34\right)^2.\]
Therefore,
\[P=3\cdot\frac14\cdot\frac9{16}=\boxed{\frac{27}{64}}.\]

The cylindrical part has radius \(r\) and height \(l\), so its volume is \(\pi r^2l\). The hemisphere contributes \(\frac12\left(\frac43\pi r^3\right)=\frac23\pi r^3\). Adding gives \(V=\pi r^2l+\frac23\pi r^3=\frac{\pi r^2}{3}(2r+3l)\), option A.
Since \(3^2=9\), the equation gives \(3^{n-2}+9=36\), hence \(3^{n-2}=27=3^3\). Therefore \(n-2=3\), so \(n=5\). Choose C.
Let the smallest integer be \(n\); the largest is \(n+3\). Then \(3n=2(n+3)\), so \(n=6\). The largest is \(9\), option B.

Each of the four equal circles has area \(9\pi\), hence radius \(3\). Their centres form a square of side \(6\). Its centre is \(3\sqrt2\) from each large-circle centre. If the small radius is \(r\), tangency gives \(r+3=3\sqrt2\). Its diameter is \(2r=6\sqrt2-6\), option D.

The triangle's right-hand interior angle is \(180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ\). The crossing angle inside the triangle is vertical to the marked \(8x+4\), so it equals \(8x+4\). Thus \((3x-6)+50+(8x+4)=180\), giving \(x=12\). The angle at A is \(3x-6=30^\circ\), option A.
If \(A\%\) of \(B\) is \(C\), then \(AB/100=C\). The percentage that \(C\) is of \(AB\) is \(100C/(AB)=100(AB/100)/(AB)=1\%\). Choose D.
Since \(p^q=1\) with positive integers, \(p=1\). Then \(q^1=4-q\), so \(2q=4\) and \(q=2\). Choose C.
Each book costs \(x/20\) dollars. Thus \(70\) books cost \(70(x/20)=7x/2\) dollars. Choose A.

A total of \(12\) requires both dice to show \(6\). Since one die is fair, the other die's probability of \(6\) is \( (1/18)/(1/6)=1/3\). Its other five outcomes are equally likely, so \(P(1)=(1-1/3)/5=2/15\). A total of \(2\) requires both dice to show \(1\), giving \( (1/6)(2/15)=1/45\). Choose B.

(1) Two equal adjacent sides and equal area can still give different supplementary included angles, so congruence is not forced. (2) With one side and its included angle fixed, equal areas force the other adjacent side to be equal; SAS then gives congruence. (3) Equal corresponding angles make the triangles similar, and equal areas force the similarity scale factor to be \(1\), hence congruence. All three imply it; choose H.
Let \(t\) be the number of tomatoes and \(c\) the number of cabbages. Then \(t+c=10\) and \(8t+12c=104\). Subtracting \(8(t+c)=80\) leaves \(4c=24\), so Jerry bought \(6\) cabbages. Choose C.

The volume of a cone is \(\frac13\pi r^2h\). Using radius \(x\) and height \(2x\),
\[V_{\text{cone}}=\frac13\pi x^2(2x)=\frac23\pi x^3.\]
Let the sphere's radius be \(R\). Its volume is \(\frac43\pi R^3\). Equating the volumes:
\[\frac43\pi R^3=\frac23\pi x^3.\]
Cancel common factors:
\[2R^3=x^3\implies R^3=\frac{x^3}{2}.\]
Taking cube roots gives
\[\boxed{R=\frac{x}{\sqrt[3]{2}}}.\]

Joining midpoints of a square produces a square with half its area. The three cube-face areas are therefore \(1,2,4\) square centimetres. Their separate surface areas sum to \(6(1+2+4)=42\). At each join, two faces are hidden over areas \(1\) and \(2\). The exposed area is \(42-2(1+2)=36\text{ cm}^2\), option D.

Arrange the numbers as \(a\le b\le c\le d\le e\), where \(c\) is the median. The range condition gives \(e-a=20\), so \(a=e-20\ge c-20\). Also, \(b\ge a\) and \(d,e\ge c\). Because the mean is zero,
\[0=a+b+c+d+e\ge2a+3c\ge2(c-20)+3c.\]
Therefore,
\[0\ge5c-40\implies c\le8.\]
This bound is attainable with the numbers \(-12,-12,8,8,8\). Their sum is zero, their range is \(20\), and their median is \(8\). Hence the maximum median is \(\boxed{8}\).

From the number line, \(q<-2<r<s<-1<t<0=u\). Thus \(qu=0\), while \(qr\) is positive and exceeds \(2|r|\). The other positive products are smaller: \(qt<|q|<qr\) since \(|t|<1<|r|\); \(rs<2|r|<qr\) since \(|s|<2<|q|\); and \(st<2<qr\). Therefore \(qr\) is largest. Choose D.

The fraction inside is \(\frac{9x^4y^{-6}}{8x^{12}y^3}=\frac{9}{8x^8y^9}\). Raising to \(-2\) reciprocates and squares, giving \(\left(\frac{8x^8y^9}{9}\right)^2=\frac{64x^{16}y^{18}}{81}\). Choose C.
The slope of \(f\) through \((1,1)\) and \((2,3)\) is \((3-1)/(2-1)=2\). Parallel line \(g\) has slope \(2\); through \((-1,2)\), it is \(y-2=2(x+1)\), or \(g(x)=2x+4\). Choose E.

An even product requires at least one even integer. An even sum requires an even number of odd integers, so among four integers the number of even integers must be even. Zero evens is impossible because the product would be odd; therefore the possible counts are \(2\) and \(4\), statements II and III. Choose D.
Apply Pythagoras: \((x+3)^2+(6x)^2=(7x-3)^2\). Expanding and cancelling \(9\) gives \(37x^2+6x=49x^2-42x\), so \(12x(x-4)=0\). Lengths require \(x>0\), hence \(x=4\). Choose B.

Basket A contains \(12\) fruits, including \(6\) oranges. The probability of drawing two oranges without replacement is
\[P_A=\frac{\binom62}{\binom{12}2}=\frac{15}{66}=\frac5{22}.\]
Basket B contains \(15\) fruits, including \(5\) apples and \(6\) lemons. The probability of selecting one apple and one lemon is
\[P_B=\frac{\binom51\binom61}{\binom{15}2}=\frac{30}{105}=\frac27.\]
The draws from different baskets are independent, so
\[P=P_A P_B=\frac5{22}\times\frac27=\boxed{\frac5{77}}.\]
The prime factorization is \(910=2\cdot5\cdot7\cdot13\). It is not divisible by \(3\), since its digit sum is \(10\). Choose B.
At \(9{:}20\), the minute hand is at \(20\times6^\circ=120^\circ\), and the hour hand is at \(9\times30^\circ+20\times0.5^\circ=280^\circ\). The smaller angle is \(280-120=160^\circ\). Choose A.

The distance from the square's centre to a corner is half its diagonal: \(AM=\frac{4\sqrt2}{2}=2\sqrt2\). The vertical height \(VM\) is perpendicular to the base. In right triangle \(VMA\), \(VM^2=VA^2-AM^2=8^2-(2\sqrt2)^2=56\). Thus \(VM=2\sqrt{14}\) cm, option A.
A number divisible by both \(11\) and \(23\) is divisible by their product \(253\). Since \(2137=8(253)+113\), the smallest addition to reach the next multiple is \(253-113=140\). Choose E.
The least common multiple of \(7\) and \(13\) is \(91\). Dividing \(6789\) by \(91\) leaves remainder \(55\), so the least addition to reach a multiple is \(91-55=36\). Choose D.
Group the terms with common factor \(190\): \(189+190\cdot191-188\cdot190=189+190(191-188)=189+570=759\). Choose C.
Factor the denominator and numerator: \(5x^2+17x+6=(5x+2)(x+3)\) and \(x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3)\). Thus \(4-\frac{17(x-3)}{5x+2}=\frac{4(5x+2)-17(x-3)}{5x+2}=\frac{3x+59}{5x+2}\). Choose C.

Let the original share price be \(P\). After the first \(20\%\) decrease, it becomes \(0.8P\). A further \(25\%\) decrease leaves
\[0.8P\times0.75=0.6P.\]
To recover the original price, the share must gain
\[P-0.6P=0.4P.\]
The required percentage increase is measured relative to the current price, not the original price:
\[\frac{0.4P}{0.6P}\times100\%=\frac23\times100\%=\boxed{66\frac23\%}.\]
The negative square root of \(81\) is \(-9\). The greatest even integer strictly less than \(-9\) is \(-10\). Choose C.
Factor \(a^2+2a-3=(a+3)(a-1)\) and \(2a+6=2(a+3)\). Since \(a>1\), cancellation is valid, giving the ratio \(2/(a-1)\). Choose C.

The smaller circle's diameter is the square's side \(s\), so its radius is \(s/2\). The larger circle's diameter is the square's diagonal \(s\sqrt2\), so its radius is \(s/\sqrt2\). Their area ratio is \(\pi(s/\sqrt2)^2:\pi(s/2)^2=\frac{s^2}{2}:\frac{s^2}{4}=2:1\), option B.

The asset identifies the chord as \(PQ\), and the radii \(OP,OQ\) meet at a right angle. Thus \(PQ^2=OP^2+OQ^2=2r^2\). With \(PQ=4\sqrt2\), \(32=2r^2\), so \(r=4\). The circumference is \(2\pi r=8\pi\), option D.

The line passes through \(5,0\) and \(0,-2\), so its slope is \(\frac{0-(-2)}{5-0}=\frac{2}{5}\) and its \(y\)-intercept is \(-2\). Thus \(y=\frac{2}{5}x-2\). For \(10,2\), this gives \(y=4-2=2\), so the point lies on the line. Choose E.
Substitute successively: \(r=3s=15t=30u\), \(s=5t=10u\), and \(t=2u\). Therefore \(\frac{rst}{u^3}=\frac{(30u)(10u)(2u)}{u^3}=600\), since \(u\neq0\). Choose E.
The ratio has \(11-4=7\) parts between penguins and sea lions. Those 7 parts equal 84, so one part is \(84/7=12\). The number of sea lions is \(4\cdot12=48\). Choose C.

The three equal squares form an L-shape with 8 exposed side-lengths around its perimeter (the shared sides are internal). Thus each square has side \(40/8=5\). The area is \(3\cdot5^2=75\) square units. Choose B.

The original mean is \(7.8\) and variance is approximately \(3.71^2=13.76\). Adding one value increases the variance only if its squared distance from 7.8 exceeds \(6(13.76)/5\), or about \(16.51\); thus the value must be more than about \(4.06\) from 7.8. Among the choices, only \(3.7\) is that far away (difference \(4.1\)). Therefore the standard deviation increases. Choose E.

Because \(R,T,V\) are collinear, \(\angle RVU=\angle TVU=60^\circ\). This inscribed angle subtends arc \(RU\), so the central angle \(RTU\) is \(120^\circ\). Since \(S,T,U\) are collinear, \(\angle RTS=180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ\). Chord \(RS\) therefore has length \(2(3)\sin(60^\circ/2)=3\), so choose C.
There are 6 ordered outcomes summing to 7: \((1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1)\). Two fair dice have \(6\cdot6=36\) equally likely ordered outcomes, so the probability is \(6/36=1/6\). Choose B.
One house requires \(10\cdot3=30\) worker-days. Four houses require \(4\cdot30=120\) worker-days. With 15 workers, the time is \(120/15=8\) days. Choose C.

Express each base as powers of \(2\) and \(5\):
\[10=2\cdot5,\quad20=2^2\cdot5,\quad8=2^3,\quad125=5^3.\]
Substituting these factorizations and collecting exponents gives
\[2^{c-2d+4c+2d-3c}\cdot5^{c-2d+2c+d-3c-3d}.\]
Simplifying,
\[=2^{2c}5^{-4d}.\]
For this expression to be an integer, both prime exponents must be nonnegative:
\[2c\ge0,\qquad-4d\ge0.\]
Since \(c\) and \(d\) are nonzero integers, the conditions are
\[\boxed{c>0\text{ and }d<0}.\]

First substitute \(c=\frac13\) into the formula for \(b\):
\[b=\frac{\sqrt5}{1/3}=3\sqrt5.\]
Since \(a=b^3\),
\[a=(3\sqrt5)^3=27(\sqrt5)^3.\]
Using \((\sqrt5)^3=5\sqrt5\),
\[a=27\cdot5\sqrt5=135\sqrt5.\]
Evaluating numerically,
\[a\approx\boxed{301.87}.\]

First expand the squared denominator:
\[(2de^3f)^2=4d^2e^6f^2.\]
Substitute this into the fraction:
\[\frac{4d^3e^4f^2}{4d^2e^6f^2}.\]
Cancel the common numerical factors and subtract exponents of matching variables:
\[d^{3-2}e^{4-6}f^{2-2}=de^{-2}.\]
Therefore,
\[\boxed{de^{-2}=\frac{d}{e^2}}.\]

The arc has length \(12\pi\), which is \(\frac34\) of the circumference. Therefore,
\[C=12\pi\div\frac34=16\pi.\]
Using \(C=2\pi r\), the radius is \(r=8\). The arc subtends \(270^\circ\), so the smaller central angle between its endpoints is \(90^\circ\). The shortest distance is the chord joining the endpoints. By the Pythagorean theorem,
\[d^2=8^2+8^2=128.\]
Thus,
\[\boxed{d=8\sqrt2}.\]

Dividing the original cube into \(8=2^3\) equal smaller cubes halves each edge length. Each small cube therefore has side \(\frac b2\) and surface area
\[6\left(\frac b2\right)^2=\frac32b^2.\]
The combined surface area of all eight small cubes is
\[8\times\frac32b^2=12b^2.\]
The original cube has surface area \(6b^2\). The increase is
\[12b^2-6b^2=\boxed{6b^2}.\]

Write \(DE=4k\) and \(EF=9k\). Since \(DF=2\), \(13k=2\), giving \(k=\frac2{13}\). The midpoint of \(EF\) is another \(\frac92k\) beyond \(E\). Its distance from \(D\) is \(4k+\frac92k=\frac{17}{2}k=\frac{17}{13}\), option E.

Substitute \(s-1\) into the function:
\[f(s-1)=(s-1)^2+2(s-1)-2.\]
Expand and simplify:
\[=s^2-2s+1+2s-2-2=s^2-3.\]
Since \(f(s-1)=1\),
\[s^2-3=1\implies s^2=4.\]
Therefore \(s=2\) or \(s=-2\). The smallest possible value is
\[\boxed{-2}.\]

Expand the cube using
\[(ax+b)^3=a^3x^3+3a^2bx^2+3ab^2x+b^3.\]
Compare coefficients with \(8x^3-px^2+18x-3\sqrt3\). From the cubic term,
\[a^3=8\implies a=2.\]
From the constant term,
\[b^3=-3\sqrt3\implies b=-\sqrt3.\]
The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(3a^2b=-p\). Hence,
\[-p=3(2)^2(-\sqrt3)=-12\sqrt3,\]
so
\[\boxed{p=12\sqrt3}.\]

It is easier to calculate the complement of getting at least two heads: getting zero or exactly one head. Five fair coin tosses have
\[2^5=32\]
equally likely outcomes. There is \(\binom50=1\) way to get zero heads and \(\binom51=5\) ways to get exactly one head. Therefore,
\[P(\text{at least two heads})=1-\frac{1+5}{32}.\]
Simplifying,
\[=\frac{26}{32}=\boxed{\frac{13}{16}}.\]

A committee of eight must contain exactly six seniors. There are \(8\) seniors and \(12-8=4\) other members. Choose six of the eight seniors:
\[\binom86=28.\]
The remaining two committee positions must be filled by nonseniors:
\[\binom42=6.\]
Multiply the independent selection counts:
\[\binom86\binom42=28\times6=\boxed{168}.\]

Men make up \(40\%\) of the club. Since \(\frac25\) of the men play cricket, the proportion of all members who are male cricket players is
\[\frac25\times\frac25=\frac4{25}.\]
Men constitute \(\frac13\) of cricket players because \(\frac23\) are women. Therefore, the total proportion playing cricket is
\[\frac4{25}\div\frac13=\frac{12}{25}.\]
Female cricket players account for
\[\frac23\times\frac{12}{25}=\frac8{25}.\]
Since women make up \(\frac35=\frac{15}{25}\) of the club, the proportion of women playing tennis is
\[\frac{15}{25}-\frac8{25}=\boxed{\frac7{25}}.\]

An absolute value is always nonnegative, so its minimum possible value is zero. Set the expression inside the absolute value equal to zero:
\[16-(x+5)^2=0.\]
Rearrange:
\[(x+5)^2=16.\]
Taking both square roots gives
\[x+5=\pm4.\]
Therefore, \(x=-9\) or \(x=-1\) makes the expression zero. Among the supplied choices, the qualifying value is
\[\boxed{x=-9}.\]

Let the one-way distance be \(d\) miles and the return speed be \(v\) miles per hour. The total distance is \(2d\), while the total travel time is
\[\frac d{21}+\frac d v.\]
Using the average speed formula,
\[26.25=\frac{2d}{d/21+d/v}=\frac2{1/21+1/v}.\]
Rearrange:
\[\frac1{21}+\frac1v=\frac2{26.25}=\frac8{105}.\]
Thus,
\[\frac1v=\frac8{105}-\frac5{105}=\frac3{105}=\frac1{35}.\]
Therefore, the return speed is \(\boxed{35\text{ mph}}\).

The mean of six numbers is \(3\), so their total sum is
\[6\times3=18.\]
The mean of the smallest and largest numbers is \(5\), so these two numbers sum to
\[2\times5=10.\]
Consequently, the other four numbers must have sum
\[18-10=8.\]
Check the four-number sums. The sequences \((-4,0,5,7)\), \((0,0,0,8)\), \((\frac12,\frac32,1,5)\), and \((1,2,2,3)\) all sum to \(8\). However,
\[1+1+1+1=4\neq8.\]
Therefore, \((1,1,1,1)\) cannot be the remaining four numbers.

The statement claims that every whole number of the form \(6k-1\) or \(6k-5\) is prime. To disprove it, identify numbers below \(50\) that have either form but are not prime. These are:
\[1,\quad25,\quad35,\quad49.\]
The number \(1\) is not prime, and the others are composite:
\[25=5^2,\qquad35=5\cdot7,\qquad49=7^2.\]
All four satisfy the stated numerical condition. Therefore, there are \(\boxed{4}\) counterexamples.

Let the square base have side \(w\); the height is \(2w\). The marked space diagonal satisfies \(d^2=w^2+w^2+(2w)^2=6w^2\), so \(w=d/\sqrt6\). The volume is \(2w^3=2(d/\sqrt6)^3=\frac{d^3\sqrt6}{18}\), option E.

Because \(EG\parallel DH\), triangles \(FEG\) and \(FDH\) are similar. The marked lengths give \(FE=4\) and \(FD=4+1=5\). Areas scale as the square of corresponding lengths, so \(\frac{[FDH]}{[FEG]}=(\frac54)^2=\frac{25}{16}\). Hence \([FDH]=\frac{25a}{16}\), option E.

The triangular base is right-angled because \(5^2+12^2=13^2\). Its area is \(\frac12(5)(12)=30\), and its perimeter is \(30\). For prism length \(l\), the surface area is \(2(30)+30l=360\), so \(l=10\). The volume is \(30(10)=300\), option C.

For a rational function, the excluded domain values are the zeros of its denominator. The panvoid is the sum of the excluded integers. For the first function, \(x^2-4=0\) gives \(-2,2\), whose sum is \(0\). For the second, \(x^3-x=x(x-1)(x+1)\) excludes \(-1,0,1\), also summing to \(0\). The third excludes \(-3,3\), and the fourth excludes only \(0\); both panvoids are \(0\). For the fifth function,
\[x^2-x=x(x-1)=0\]
when \(x=0\) or \(x=1\). Its panvoid is
\[0+1=\boxed{1}.\]
This is the only function with a different panvoid.

Solve the simultaneous equations:
\[3s+5t=10,\qquad2s-t=7.\]
From the second equation,
\[t=2s-7.\]
Substitute into the first:
\[3s+5(2s-7)=10\implies13s=45,\]
so \(s=\frac{45}{13}\). Then
\[t=2\cdot\frac{45}{13}-7=-\frac1{13}.\]
Evaluate the requested expression:
\[\frac12s+3t=\frac{45}{26}-\frac3{13}=\frac{39}{26}=\boxed{1.5}.\]

Start with
\[p=\frac{\sqrt q+z}{r^2+z}.\]
Multiply by the denominator:
\[p(r^2+z)=\sqrt q+z.\]
Expand and collect terms involving \(z\):
\[pr^2+pz=\sqrt q+z,\]
\[pz-z=\sqrt q-pr^2.\]
Factor out \(z\):
\[z(p-1)=\sqrt q-pr^2.\]
Dividing by \(p-1\), provided it is nonzero, gives
\[\boxed{z=\frac{\sqrt q-pr^2}{p-1}}.\]

The total surface area of a closed cylinder is
\[A=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh,\]
while its volume is
\[V=\pi r^2h.\]
Since these quantities are numerically equal,
\[2\pi r^2+2\pi rh=\pi r^2h.\]
Divide by \(\pi r\), where \(r>0\):
\[2r+2h=rh.\]
Collect the terms containing \(h\):
\[rh-2h=2r\implies h(r-2)=2r.\]
Therefore,
\[\boxed{h=\frac{2r}{r-2}}.\]

Let the capacities of the larger and smaller containers be \(L\) and \(S\), where \(L>S\). Initially, the total water volume is \(L\). When both containers hold the same volume \(v\), conservation of water gives
\[2v=L\implies v=\frac L2.\]
The fraction of the larger container filled is
\[p=\frac vL=\frac12.\]
For the smaller container,
\[q=\frac vS=\frac{L}{2S}.\]
Because \(L>S\),
\[\frac{L}{2S}>\frac12.\]
Hence, \(\boxed{p=0.5\text{ and }q>0.5}\).

If the original side is \(s\), an inner side joins points separated by perpendicular distances \(s/3\) and \(2s/3\). Its squared length is \(s^2/9+4s^2/9=5s^2/9\). Each new square therefore has \(\frac59\) of the previous area. The fourth square follows three reductions, giving \((\frac59)^3=\frac{125}{729}\), option C.

Since \(BC\parallel DE\), triangles \(ABC\) and \(ADE\) are similar. Their side ratios give \(\frac{4}{4+(x-4)}=\frac{x}{x+3}\), so \(4(x+3)=x^2\). Hence \((x-6)(x+2)=0\). Lengths are positive, so \(x=6\), and \(DE=x+3=9\) cm. Choose C.

The cylinder has radius \(r\) and height \(2r\), since its height equals the sphere's diameter. Its volume is
\[V_c=\pi r^2(2r)=2\pi r^3.\]
The sphere's volume is
\[V_s=\frac43\pi r^3.\]
The fraction of the cylinder occupied by the sphere is the ratio of their volumes:
\[\frac{V_s}{V_c}=\frac{\frac43\pi r^3}{2\pi r^3}=\boxed{\frac23}.\]

The shaded regions are the largest circle minus the third, plus the second minus the smallest. Using their diameters, the area is \(\frac{\pi}{4}[(4d)^2-(3d)^2+(2d)^2-d^2]=\frac{\pi d^2}{4}(16-9+4-1)=\frac52\pi d^2\), option A.

Apply the definition \(y\diamond x=\frac{y^x}{x}\) to the expression inside the parentheses:
\[2\diamond3=\frac{2^3}{3}=\frac83.\]
Now apply the same operation rule to the result and \(2\):
\[\left(\frac83\right)\diamond2=\frac{\left(\frac83\right)^2}{2}.\]
Square the fraction and divide by \(2\):
\[\frac{\frac{64}{9}}{2}=\boxed{\frac{32}{9}}.\]

Start with
\[y=5\left(\frac{x}{2}-3\right)^2-10.\]
Add \(10\) to both sides and divide by \(5\):
\[\frac{y+10}{5}=\left(\frac{x}{2}-3\right)^2.\]
Take both positive and negative square roots:
\[\frac{x}{2}-3=\pm\sqrt{\frac{y+10}{5}}.\]
Add \(3\) and multiply by \(2\):
\[\boxed{x=6\pm2\sqrt{\frac{y+10}{5}}}.\]

The total number of balls is \(x+y+z\). Therefore, the probability of selecting a red ball first is
\[P(R)=\frac{x}{x+y+z}.\]
Because the first ball is replaced, the total and the colour proportions remain unchanged. Thus, the probability of selecting a blue ball second is
\[P(B)=\frac{y}{x+y+z}.\]
The selections are independent, so multiply their probabilities:
\[P(R\text{ then }B)=\frac{x}{x+y+z}\cdot\frac{y}{x+y+z}=\boxed{\frac{xy}{(x+y+z)^2}}.\]

The function \(f(t)=t^{3/5}=(\sqrt[5]{t})^3\) is strictly increasing for all real \(t\). Taking a fifth root preserves the order of two real numbers because the root index is odd. Cubing also preserves their order. Therefore,
\[x^{3/5}<y^{3/5}\implies x<y.\]
This condition is sufficient regardless of whether \(x\) and \(y\) are positive or negative.

A point must satisfy both inequalities:
\[y\ge x^2+3,\qquad x\ge\frac1y.\]
For the point \((1,6)\), substitute \(x=1\) and \(y=6\). The first inequality becomes
\[6\ge1^2+3=4,\]
which is true. The second becomes
\[1\ge\frac16,\]
which is also true. Therefore, \(\boxed{(1,6)}\) lies in the required region.

Group the factors before expanding:
\[(\sqrt5-\sqrt2)^2(\sqrt5+\sqrt2)^2=\left[(\sqrt5-\sqrt2)(\sqrt5+\sqrt2)\right]^2.\]
Use the difference-of-squares identity \((a-b)(a+b)=a^2-b^2\):
\[=\left[(\sqrt5)^2-(\sqrt2)^2\right]^2.\]
Simplify:
\[=(5-2)^2=3^2=\boxed{9}.\]
The marked horizontal and vertical sides are perpendicular. Therefore \(A=\frac12(4+\sqrt2)(2-\sqrt2)=\frac12(8-2\sqrt2-2)=3-\sqrt2\text{ cm}^2\), option C.

The shape comprises an equilateral triangle of side \(x\) and a semicircle with diameter \(x\). Their areas are \(\frac{\sqrt3}{4}x^2\) and \(\frac12\pi(x/2)^2=\frac{\pi x^2}{8}\). Adding gives \(\frac{x^2(2\sqrt3+\pi)}{8}\), option A.

Square the entire fraction by squaring its numerator and denominator:
\[\left(\frac{2x^{3/2}y^3}{\sqrt z}\right)^2=\frac{2^2(x^{3/2})^2(y^3)^2}{(\sqrt z)^2}.\]
Apply the power rule \((a^m)^n=a^{mn}\):
\[(x^{3/2})^2=x^3,\qquad(y^3)^2=y^6.\]
Also, \(2^2=4\) and \((\sqrt z)^2=z\). Therefore,
\[\boxed{\frac{4x^3y^6}{z}}.\]

To determine whether the curves \(y=1-x^2\) and \(y=x+6\) intersect, set their expressions for \(y\) equal:
\[1-x^2=x+6.\]
Rearrange:
\[x^2+x+5=0.\]
A quadratic equation has real solutions only when its discriminant is nonnegative. Here,
\[\Delta=b^2-4ac=1^2-4(1)(5)=-19.\]
Since \(\Delta<0\), the equation has no real solutions. Therefore, these two graphs do not intersect.

The general term is
\[a_n=\frac{n}{n+1}.\]
Replace \(n\) with \(n+1\) to obtain the next term:
\[a_{n+1}=\frac{n+1}{n+2}.\]
Subtract the current term from the next term:
\[a_{n+1}-a_n=\frac{n+1}{n+2}-\frac{n}{n+1}.\]
Use the common denominator \((n+2)(n+1)\):
\[=\frac{(n+1)^2-n(n+2)}{(n+2)(n+1)}.\]
The numerator simplifies to \(n^2+2n+1-n^2-2n=1\). Thus,
\[\boxed{\frac1{(n+2)(n+1)}}.\]

Let the two roots be \(r_1\) and \(r_2\). A monic quadratic equation with these roots is
\[(x-r_1)(x-r_2)=0.\]
Expanding gives
\[x^2-(r_1+r_2)x+r_1r_2=0.\]
The sum of the roots is \(7\), and their product is \(9\). Substitute these values:
\[\boxed{x^2-7x+9=0}.\]

From \(x>y^2\) and \(y^2\ge0\), we know \(x>0\). Since \(x<z\), it follows that \(z>x>0\), so \(z\) is positive. The remaining inequality gives
\[y^2<z^2.\]
Taking square roots of both nonnegative quantities yields
\[|y|<|z|.\]
Because \(z>0\), we have \(|z|=z\). Thus,
\[-z<y<z.\]
In particular, \(\boxed{y<z}\), which must always hold.

Substitute \(x=4.6\times10^7\) and \(y=2\times10^6\):
\[\frac{x+7y}{x-2y}=\frac{4.6\times10^7+7(2\times10^6)}{4.6\times10^7-2(2\times10^6)}.\]
Express all terms in millions:
\[=\frac{46+14}{46-4}=\frac{60}{42}.\]
Divide the numerator and denominator by \(6\):
\[\boxed{\frac{10}{7}}.\]
The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord, so \(DB=16/2=8\). In right triangle \(ODB\), \(OD=\sqrt{OB^2-DB^2}=\sqrt{10^2-8^2}=6\). Since \(OC=10\), \(CD=OC-OD=10-6=4\), option B.

Start with
\[6x^2-x-15=0.\]
Find two numbers whose product is \(6(-15)=-90\) and whose sum is \(-1\): these are \(9\) and \(-10\). Split the middle term:
\[6x^2+9x-10x-15=0.\]
Factor by grouping:
\[3x(2x+3)-5(2x+3)=0,\]
\[(2x+3)(3x-5)=0.\]
Set each factor equal to zero:
\[2x+3=0\implies x=-\frac32,\]
\[3x-5=0\implies x=\frac53.\]
Hence, \(\boxed{x=-\frac32\text{ or }x=\frac53}\).

Rewrite the transformed function as
\[g(x)=a f(x+h),\qquad f(x)=x^2.\]
Replacing \(x\) with \(x+h\) translates the parabola horizontally by \(h\) units to the left when \(h>0\). Multiplying the function by \(a\) multiplies all its vertical coordinates by \(a\), producing a vertical scaling. Thus the transformation consists of a horizontal translation and a vertical scaling by \(a\). If \(a<0\), there is also a reflection across the horizontal axis.

Let the cube's side length be \(s\). Its surface area is \(6s^2\), and its volume is \(s^3\). Since these have the same numerical value,
\[6s^2=s^3.\]
A cube has positive side length, so divide by \(s^2\):
\[s=6.\]
Calculate its volume:
\[V=s^3=6^3=\boxed{216\text{ cubic units}}.\]

A fair coin has probability \(\frac12\) of landing heads. A standard die has four numbers greater than \(2\): \(3,4,5,6\). Therefore,
\[P(\text{number}>2)=\frac46=\frac23.\]
The coin toss and die roll are independent, so multiply their probabilities:
\[P(\text{heads and number}>2)=\frac12\times\frac23=\boxed{\frac13}.\]

For Box B to produce a white marble labeled A, a white marble must first be transferred from Box A. The probability of this is
\[P(\text{transfer white})=\frac3{10}.\]
After the transfer, Box B contains \(11\) marbles, exactly one of which is the transferred white marble labeled A. The probability of drawing that particular marble is \(\frac1{11}\). Multiply the probabilities of the two required events:
\[P=\frac3{10}\times\frac1{11}=\boxed{\frac3{110}}.\]

The middle triangle has perpendicular sides \(15,20\), hence hypotenuse \(\sqrt{15^2+20^2}=25\). By the corresponding sides in the similar triangles, \(\frac{b}{15}=\frac{15}{25}\), so \(b=9\). Also \(\frac{a}{25}=\frac{25}{15}\), so \(a=\frac{125}{3}\). Thus \(a-b=\frac{125}{3}-9=\frac{98}{3}\), option E.

Let the value of the infinitely nested radical be \(R\):
\[R=\sqrt{x+\sqrt{x+\sqrt{x+\cdots}}}.\]
Because the expression repeats indefinitely, the radical inside the first square root is also \(R\). Therefore,
\[R=\sqrt{x+R}.\]
Given \(R=4\), substitute:
\[4=\sqrt{x+4}.\]
Square both sides:
\[16=x+4.\]
Subtract \(4\):
\[\boxed{x=12}.\]

The pyramid has square base area \(s^2\) and height \(h\), so its volume is
\[V_p=\frac13s^2h.\]
The largest cone fitted inside has its base circle inscribed in the square, giving radius \(r=\frac s2\), and has height \(h\). Its volume is
\[V_c=\frac13\pi\left(\frac s2\right)^2h=\frac{\pi s^2h}{12}.\]
Subtract the cone's volume from the pyramid's volume:
\[V_p-V_c=\frac{s^2h}{3}-\frac{\pi s^2h}{12}.\]
Factor the expression:
\[\boxed{\frac{s^2h}{3}\left(1-\frac\pi4\right)}.\]

The Lions have won \(1\) game, while the Tigers have won \(3\). The Tigers need only one more victory, but the Lions must win three consecutive games to reach four victories first. The probability of a Lions victory in any game is \(0.3\). Assuming independent game outcomes, the probability of three consecutive Lions victories is
\[P=0.3\times0.3\times0.3=0.027.\]
Convert to a percentage:
\[0.027\times100\%=\boxed{2.7\%}.\]

For an equilateral triangle, its circumradius is twice its inradius, so each new inscribed circle has half the previous radius. The third triangle lies in a circle of radius \(R/4\). An equilateral triangle inscribed in a circle of radius \(\rho\) has side \(\rho\sqrt3\). Its side is therefore \(R\sqrt3/4\), option A.

Find the greatest common factor of \(392\) and \(420\) using the Euclidean algorithm. Subtract the smaller number from the larger:
\[420-392=28.\]
Both original numbers are divisible by \(28\):
\[392=28\times14,\qquad420=28\times15.\]
Since \(14\) and \(15\) are consecutive integers, they have no common factor greater than \(1\). Therefore,
\[\gcd(392,420)=28\gcd(14,15)=\boxed{28}.\]

Let \(N=0.181818\ldots\), where the block \(18\) repeats indefinitely. Multiply by \(100\) to shift the decimal point by two places:
\[100N=18.181818\ldots\]
Subtract the original equation:
\[100N-N=18.181818\ldots-0.181818\ldots\]
The repeating decimal parts cancel, giving
\[99N=18.\]
Therefore,
\[N=\frac{18}{99}=\boxed{\frac2{11}}.\]

First calculate the slope of the line through \((1,-4)\) and \((3,2)\):
\[m=\frac{2-(-4)}{3-1}=\frac62=3.\]
Use the point-slope equation with \((1,-4)\):
\[y+4=3(x-1).\]
Expand and simplify:
\[y=3x-7.\]
At the \(x\)-intercept, \(y=0\), so
\[0=3x-7\implies x=\frac73.\]
Thus, the intercept is
\[\boxed{\left(\frac73,0\right)}.\]

The angles sum to \(180^\circ\): \((6x+6)+(4x-10)+(5x+4)=180\), so \(15x=180\) and \(x=12\). The angles are then \(78^\circ,38^\circ,64^\circ\). Their largest difference is \(78^\circ-38^\circ=40^\circ\), option D.

An isosceles right triangle has two equal perpendicular legs. Let each leg have length \(a\). By the Pythagorean theorem,
\[a^2+a^2=12^2.\]
Therefore,
\[2a^2=144\implies a^2=72.\]
The area of a right triangle is half the product of its perpendicular legs:
\[A=\frac12a\cdot a=\frac12a^2.\]
Hence,
\[A=\frac12\times72=\boxed{36\text{ cm}^2}.\]

Let the three numbers be \(2k\), \(3k\), and \(5k\), following their ratio \(2:3:5\). The smallest number is \(16\), so
\[2k=16\implies k=8.\]
The three numbers are therefore
\[2k=16,\qquad3k=24,\qquad5k=40.\]
Their sum is
\[16+24+40=\boxed{80}.\]

Group the terms to form a perfect square:
\[4x^2-y^2+4x+1=(4x^2+4x+1)-y^2.\]
Recognize that
\[4x^2+4x+1=(2x+1)^2.\]
The expression becomes
\[(2x+1)^2-y^2.\]
Use the difference-of-squares identity \(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\):
\[=(2x+1-y)(2x+1+y).\]
Therefore,
\[\boxed{(2x-y+1)(2x+y+1)}.\]

The function is \(f(x)=-(2^{x+1})\). It is always negative, has \(f(0)=-2\), approaches \(0\) from below as \(x\) decreases, and decreases rapidly as \(x\) increases. Graph D has this intercept and behaviour. Choose D.

The polygon has eight equal sides, so the angle between radii to consecutive vertices is \(360^\circ/8=45^\circ\). The marked radii span three such intervals. Therefore \(x=3(45^\circ)=135^\circ\), option D.

Three positive lengths form a right triangle if the squares of the two shorter sides sum to the square of the longest side. For the first set,
\[8^2+15^2=64+225=289=17^2.\]
For the second set,
\[7^2+24^2=49+576=625=25^2.\]
Both satisfy the Pythagorean theorem. For the third set,
\[9^2+40^2=81+1600=1681=41^2\neq42^2.\]
Therefore, only the first two sets form right triangles.

Start with
\[2x^2-5=5x-2.\]
Move every term to the left:
\[2x^2-5x-3=0.\]
Factor the quadratic:
\[(2x+1)(x-3)=0.\]
Set each factor equal to zero:
\[2x+1=0\implies x=-\frac12,\]
\[x-3=0\implies x=3.\]
Therefore,
\[\boxed{x=-\frac12\text{ or }x=3}.\]
The graph opens downwards and has vertex \((-1,6)\), so its equation has the form \(f(x)=-(x+1)^2+6\). Expanding gives \(f(x)=-x^2-2x+5\). Its intercept \(f(0)=5\) also matches the graph. Choose E.

Each question has three possible answers, only one of which is correct. A random guess therefore has probability
\[P(\text{correct})=\frac13.\]
To obtain a perfect score, all three answers must be correct. Assuming independent random guesses, multiply the probabilities:
\[P(\text{all correct})=\frac13\times\frac13\times\frac13=\left(\frac13\right)^3.\]
Hence,
\[\boxed{\frac1{27}}.\]

Find the prime factorization of each number:
\[36=2^2\cdot3^2,\]
\[48=2^4\cdot3,\]
\[60=2^2\cdot3\cdot5.\]
The least common multiple contains every prime factor raised to its highest exponent among the three factorizations. Therefore,
\[\operatorname{lcm}(36,48,60)=2^4\cdot3^2\cdot5.\]
Calculate:
\[16\times9\times5=\boxed{720}.\]

Use the equations
\[x+y+z=0,\qquad x-y=1,\qquad y-z=-2.\]
From the second equation, \(x=y+1\). From the third, \(z=y+2\). Substitute both into the first:
\[(y+1)+y+(y+2)=0.\]
Combine like terms:
\[3y+3=0\implies y=-1.\]
Then
\[x=y+1=0,\qquad z=y+2=1.\]
Thus,
\[\boxed{x=0,\quad y=-1,\quad z=1}.\]

A \(90^\circ\) clockwise rotation sends \((x,y)\) to \((y,-x)\). Reflecting this in the horizontal axis gives \((y,x)\). The original vertices are \(A(1,1),B(2,3),C(4,2)\), so the final vertices are \(A(1,1),B(3,2),C(2,4)\), option C.

Out of \(100\) students, \(15\) like neither drink. Therefore, the number who like coffee or milk or both is
\[100-15=85.\]
Use the inclusion-exclusion principle:
\[|C\cup M|=|C|+|M|-|C\cap M|.\]
Substitute the given counts:
\[85=66+32-|C\cap M|.\]
Rearrange:
\[|C\cap M|=66+32-85=\boxed{13}.\]

Start with
\[3x\left(3x^{-1/3}\right)^3.\]
Apply the power to both factors inside the parentheses:
\[\left(3x^{-1/3}\right)^3=3^3x^{(-1/3)\cdot3}=27x^{-1}.\]
Multiply by the factor outside:
\[3x\cdot27x^{-1}=81x^{1-1}.\]
Since \(x^0=1\) for nonzero \(x\), the result is
\[\boxed{81}.\]

For an arithmetic sequence, the \(n\)-th term is
\[a_n=a_1+(n-1)d,\]
where \(d\) is the common difference. Given \(a_1=8\) and \(a_{16}=-37\), substitute:
\[-37=8+15d.\]
Subtract \(8\):
\[15d=-45.\]
Divide by \(15\):
\[\boxed{d=-3}.\]

The corresponding sides \(16\) and \(24\) give scale factor \(24/16=3/2\). Thus \((x+7)(3/2)=18\), so \(x=5\). The base relation is \(2y-3=10(3/2)=15\), giving \(y=9\). Therefore \(x+y=14\), option C.

The four marked angles surround one point, so their sum is \(360^\circ\): \(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{x}{4}+\frac{x}{6}+\frac{x}{3}=360\). Using denominator \(12\), this gives \(\frac{15x}{12}=360\), hence \(x=288\). Choose B.

The first digit may be any of \(2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9\), giving \(8\) choices. Each of the remaining five digits has \(10\) choices. Therefore, the total number of valid telephone numbers is
\[8\times10^5.\]
For a number beginning with \(3\) and ending with \(5\), the first and last digits are fixed. The four middle digits each have \(10\) possibilities, giving
\[10^4\]
qualifying numbers. The required fraction is
\[\frac{10^4}{8\times10^5}=\boxed{\frac1{80}}.\]

The visible region is circular because the light reaches the same distance in every direction. Its initial radius is \(60\) miles. After the increase, the radius is
\[60+40=100\text{ miles}.\]
Using the circle-area formula, the increase in visible area is
\[\Delta A=\pi(100^2-60^2).\]
Simplify:
\[\Delta A=\pi(10000-3600)=6400\pi.\]
Numerically,
\[6400\pi\approx20106\text{ square miles}.\]
Thus the approximate increase is \(\boxed{20000\text{ square miles}}\).

Since dividing \(n\) by \(9\) leaves remainder \(5\), write
\[n=9k+5\]
for some integer \(k\). Then
\[n+29=9k+5+29=9k+34.\]
Express \(34\) as a multiple of \(9\) plus a remainder:
\[34=9\cdot3+7.\]
Therefore,
\[n+29=9(k+3)+7.\]
The remainder upon division by \(9\) is \(\boxed{7}\).
Convert the dimensions first: \(r=3(2.5)=7.5\) cm and \(h=6(2.5)=15\) cm. Then \(V=\frac13\pi r^2h=\frac13\pi(7.5)^2(15)=281.25\pi\text{ cm}^3\), option B.

A prime number is a positive integer greater than \(1\) with exactly two positive divisors: \(1\) and itself. The first six prime numbers are
\[2,\ 3,\ 5,\ 7,\ 11,\ 13.\]
Add them:
\[2+3+5+7+11+13=\boxed{41}.\]

First simplify the fraction inside the negative power:
\[\frac{2xy^{-2}y^4}{4xy}=\frac{2xy^2}{4xy}=\frac y2.\]
A power of \(-1\) means taking the reciprocal:
\[\left(\frac y2\right)^{-1}=\frac2y.\]
Simplify the second fraction:
\[\frac{xy}{2x^3y}=\frac1{2x^2}.\]
Multiply the two results:
\[\frac2y\cdot\frac1{2x^2}=\boxed{\frac1{x^2y}}.\]

The area of a triangle is
\[A=\frac12bh,\]
where \(b\) is its base and \(h\) is its height. Increasing the base by \(40\%\) multiplies it by \(1.4\), while decreasing the height by \(40\%\) multiplies it by \(0.6\). The new area is
\[A'=\frac12(1.4b)(0.6h).\]
Therefore,
\[A'=1.4\times0.6\times A=0.84A.\]
The new area is \(84\%\) of the original, so the decrease is
\[100\%-84\%=\boxed{16\%}.\]

Let \(r\) be the fraction of mixture \(R\) that is red. The mixtures are combined in the ratio \(12:5:3\), totaling \(20\) parts. The proportion of red paint is the weighted average:
\[\frac{12(0.30)+5(0.20)+3r}{20}=0.25.\]
Multiply by \(20\):
\[3.6+1+3r=5.\]
Subtract \(4.6\):
\[3r=0.4\implies r=\frac{2}{15}.\]
Convert this fraction to a percentage:
\[\frac{2}{15}\times100\%=\boxed{13\frac13\%}.\]

Start with the first term, \(1\). Each following term is twice the previous term plus \(1\):
\[a_{n+1}=2a_n+1.\]
Calculate the first five terms:
\[a_1=1,\]
\[a_2=2(1)+1=3,\]
\[a_3=2(3)+1=7,\]
\[a_4=2(7)+1=15,\]
\[a_5=2(15)+1=31.\]
Their sum is
\[1+3+7+15+31=\boxed{57}.\]

The circumference of a circle with radius \(r\) is
\[C=2\pi r.\]
Its area is
\[A=\pi r^2.\]
The requested ratio is the circumference divided by the area:
\[\frac CA=\frac{2\pi r}{\pi r^2}.\]
Cancel the common factors \(\pi\) and \(r\):
\[\boxed{\frac2r}.\]

The shaded region is an annular sector of angle \(\pi/4\). Its outer radius is \(PR=4\) ft. Since \(PT=4\) and \(ST=2\), its inner radius is \(PS=2\) ft. Its area is \(\frac{\theta}{2}(R^2-r^2)=\frac{\pi}{8}(16-4)=1.5\pi\text{ ft}^2\), option A.
The median of a trapezoid equals the average of the two parallel bases. Thus \(7x-4=\frac{38+(6x-6)}2=16+3x\). Therefore \(4x=20\) and \(x=5\). The required base is \(UV=6x-6=24\), option B.

Use the defined operation
\[a\#b\#c=\frac ac\cdot b+a\cdot c.\]
Evaluate each expression to find an odd integer:
\[4\#8\#2=\frac42\cdot8+4\cdot2=24,\]
\[3\#2\#1=\frac31\cdot2+3\cdot1=9,\]
\[9\#3\#3=\frac93\cdot3+9\cdot3=36,\]
\[8\#6\#4=\frac84\cdot6+8\cdot4=44,\]
\[5\#7\#1=\frac51\cdot7+5\cdot1=40.\]
Only \(9\) is odd, so the required expression has value \(\boxed{9}\).

Let \(c\) be the number of cabbages and \(t\) the number of tomatoes. The total number of vegetables gives
\[c+t=10.\]
Each cabbage costs \(12\) dollars and each tomato costs \(8\) dollars, so
\[12c+8t=104.\]
Substitute \(t=10-c\):
\[12c+8(10-c)=104.\]
Expand and simplify:
\[12c+80-8c=104,\]
\[4c=24.\]
Therefore,
\[\boxed{c=6}.\]

The equal sides \(EF=ED=13\) make the triangle isosceles. The perpendicular \(EG\) bisects \(FD\), so \(x+5=3x-9\), giving \(x=7\). Thus \(FG=12\). Pythagoras gives \(EG=\sqrt{13^2-12^2}=\sqrt{25}=5\), option B.

The five equal angles at the centre sum to \(360^\circ\), so \(x=72^\circ\). The two radii meeting the endpoints of the drawn chord enclose \(2x=144^\circ\). They form an isosceles triangle whose base angle is \(y=(180^\circ-144^\circ)/2=18^\circ\). Hence \(y/x=18/72=1/4\), option B.

First simplify the target expression:
\[\frac{10!}{8!}=\frac{10\cdot9\cdot8!}{8!}=90.\]
Evaluate statement I:
\[5!-4!-3!=120-24-6=90.\]
Statement II gives
\[\frac{5!}{4!}=5,\]
which is not equal to \(90\). Statement III gives
\[15(3!)=15\cdot6=90.\]
Therefore, exactly statements I and III equal the target value.

The function \(f(x)=5x-7\) has the linear form \(y=mx+b\), where \(m\) is the gradient. Here, \(m=5>0\), so increasing \(x\) by \(1\) increases \(y\) by \(5\). Therefore, its graph is a straight line that rises from left to right.

The rectangle on the right has area \(4(2)=8\). The other rectangle has the same area and its outer corner \(R\) lies in quadrant II. For \(R=(-2,4)\), its width is \(2\), height is \(4\), and area is \(8\). Among the listed points this is the quadrant-II point with the required area. Choose C.

Subtract the common terms \(\frac17+\frac18\) from both sides:
\[\frac16>\frac1x.\]
All supplied values of \(x\) are positive, so multiplying by \(6x\) preserves the inequality:
\[x>6.\]
Among the given values, only \(\boxed{x=7}\) satisfies this condition.

The operation is defined by
\[a\#b=ab+a+b.\]
Substitute \(a=2\) and \(b=5\):
\[2\#5=2\cdot5+2+5.\]
Calculate the product and then add:
\[10+2+5=\boxed{17}.\]

A root of an equation is a value of \(x\) that satisfies it. Substitute either given root into
\[3(x-7)(x-2)=k.\]
For \(x=7\), the first factor becomes zero:
\[k=3(7-7)(7-2)=0.\]
Likewise, substituting \(x=2\) makes the second factor zero. Hence,
\[\boxed{k=0}.\]

Rewrite the line as \(2x-y-1=0\). The distance from a point \((x_0,y_0)\) to this line is
\[d=\frac{|2x_0-y_0-1|}{\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2}}=\frac{|2x_0-y_0-1|}{\sqrt5}.\]
For the five supplied points, the absolute-value numerators are respectively
\[2,\quad2,\quad2,\quad4,\quad2.\]
Four points are at distance \(\frac2{\sqrt5}\), whereas \((5,13)\) is at distance \(\frac4{\sqrt5}\). Thus \(\boxed{(5,13)}\) is the point at a different distance.

Let \(V\) be the original volume of water. Freezing increases its volume by \(9\%\), so the resulting ice volume is
\[V_{\text{ice}}=1.09V.\]
To obtain \(40\text{ cm}^3\) of ice,
\[1.09V=40.\]
Divide by \(1.09\):
\[V=\frac{40}{1.09}\approx\boxed{36.7\text{ cm}^3}.\]

The internal base dimensions are determined by subtracting the steel thickness from both opposite sides of each horizontal dimension. Each side wall is \(4\text{ cm}\) thick, so the internal width is
\[48-2(4)=40\text{ cm}.\]
Similarly, the internal depth is
\[44-2(4)=36\text{ cm}.\]
The base thickness of \(8\text{ cm}\) affects the internal height, not the horizontal base dimensions. Therefore, the internal base measures \(\boxed{40\text{ cm}\times36\text{ cm}}\).

Transformation 2 rotates the triangle \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise; transformation 5 adds \(180^\circ\). Their composition is a \(270^\circ\) anticlockwise rotation, equivalent to \(90^\circ\) clockwise. It sends \(L\) to \(P\), the upward side \(LN\) to the rightward side \(PR\), and \(M\) to \(Q\), as shown. Choose D.

Square the numerator and denominator separately:
\[\left(\frac{2x^{3/2}y^3}{\sqrt z}\right)^2=\frac{2^2(x^{3/2})^2(y^3)^2}{(\sqrt z)^2}.\]
Apply the exponent rule \((a^m)^n=a^{mn}\):
\[(x^{3/2})^2=x^3,\qquad(y^3)^2=y^6.\]
Also, \(2^2=4\) and \((\sqrt z)^2=z\). Combining these results gives
\[\boxed{\frac{4x^3y^6}{z}}.\]

From the second equation,
\[2x-y=5\implies y=2x-5.\]
Substitute into the first equation:
\[4x^2+(2x-5)^2+10(2x-5)=47.\]
Expand and combine terms:
\[4x^2+4x^2-20x+25+20x-50=47,\]
\[8x^2=72\implies x^2=9.\]
Thus \(x=\pm3\). For the positive solution, \(x=3\), giving
\[y=2(3)-5=1.\]
Therefore, \(\boxed{x=3,\ y=1}\).

Let \(M\) denote being male and \(S\) studying mathematics. We know
\[P(M)=\frac25,\qquad P(S)=\frac13.\]
The required conditional probability is
\[p=P(S\mid M)=\frac{P(S\cap M)}{P(M)}.\]
Its minimum is \(0\), because all mathematics students could be female: females make up \(\frac35\) of the group, enough to include the \(\frac13\) who study mathematics. Its maximum occurs when every mathematics student is male:
\[p\le\frac{1/3}{2/5}=\frac56.\]
Hence,
\[\boxed{0\le p\le\frac56}.\]

Take the vertex as \((0,0,0)\). The centre of the opposite unit-square face is \((1,\frac12,\frac12)\). The squared distance is \(1^2+(\frac12)^2+(\frac12)^2=\frac32\). Thus the marked length is \(\sqrt{\frac32}\), option B.

The equation of a circle with centre \((h,k)\) and radius \(r\) is
\[(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2.\]
Substitute \(h=\frac32\), \(k=\frac12\), and \(r=3\):
\[\left(x-\frac32\right)^2+\left(y-\frac12\right)^2=9.\]
Expand:
\[x^2-3x+\frac94+y^2-y+\frac14=9.\]
Combine constants and rearrange:
\[x^2-3x+y^2-y-\frac{13}{2}=0.\]
Multiply by \(2\):
\[\boxed{2x^2-6x+2y^2-2y-13=0}.\]

Start with
\[\frac{x+5}{2}-\frac{2x-1}{3}=4.\]
Multiply every term by \(6\), the least common denominator:
\[3(x+5)-2(2x-1)=24.\]
Expand the brackets:
\[3x+15-4x+2=24.\]
Collect like terms:
\[-x+17=24\implies-x=7.\]
Therefore,
\[\boxed{x=-7}.\]

Factor \(3.246\times10^4\) from the numerator:
\[3.246\times10^6+3.246\times10^4=3.246\times10^4(100+1).\]
Since \(3.246=2(1.623)\), the fraction becomes
\[\frac{2(1.623)(101)\times10^4}{1.623\times10^{11}}.\]
Cancel \(1.623\) and combine powers of ten:
\[=202\times10^{-7}=2.02\times10^{-5}.\]
As an ordinary decimal, correct to three significant figures, this is
\[\boxed{0.0000202}.\]

Let each perpendicular side of the isosceles triangle be \(l\). The distance from its right-angle vertex to its hypotenuse is \(l/\sqrt2\). Tangency to the quarter-circle gives \(l/\sqrt2=r\), so the triangle has area \(l^2/2=r^2\). Subtracting the quarter-circle gives \(r^2-\pi r^2/4=(1-\pi/4)r^2\), option A.

Evaluate the numerator:
\[2\times10^3+8\times10^2=2000+800=2800.\]
Evaluate the denominator:
\[\frac1{2500}+3\times10^{-4}=0.0004+0.0003=0.0007.\]
The expression becomes
\[\sqrt{\frac{2800}{0.0007}}=\sqrt{4{,}000{,}000}.\]
Taking the square root gives
\[\boxed{2000}.\]

Start with
\[\sqrt{\frac2x+1}=y-3.\]
Square both sides:
\[\frac2x+1=(y-3)^2.\]
Subtract \(1\):
\[\frac2x=(y-3)^2-1.\]
Use the difference-of-squares identity:
\[(y-3)^2-1=(y-4)(y-2).\]
Therefore,
\[\frac2x=(y-4)(y-2),\]
and solving for \(x\) gives
\[\boxed{x=\frac2{(y-4)(y-2)}}.\]

Factor the numerator and denominator:
\[y=\frac{(x-4)(x+4)}{(x+2)(x+4)}.\]
Since \(x>-2\), the factor \(x+4\) is nonzero and can be cancelled:
\[y=\frac{x-4}{x+2}.\]
Multiply both sides by \(x+2\):
\[xy+2y=x-4.\]
Collect terms containing \(x\):
\[x-xy=2y+4.\]
Factor and divide:
\[x(1-y)=2y+4,\]
\[\boxed{x=\frac{2y+4}{1-y}}.\]

After any first move, the second move returns the counter to its start only if it has the opposite direction and exactly the same distance. Each spinner has four equal sectors, giving probabilities \(1/4\) for each requirement. The spinners are independent, so the probability is \((1/4)(1/4)=1/16\), option C.

Since \(AB\parallel CD\), triangles \(AEB\) and \(DEC\) are similar. Their corresponding sides give \(\frac{BE}{EC}=\frac{AE}{ED}=\frac25\). The diagram labels \(BE=x\) and \(EC=x+6\), so \(5x=2(x+6)\). Hence \(3x=12\), giving \(BE=4\) cm, option A.

The total running time for the first group is
\[20\times54=1080\text{ seconds}.\]
If the second group has \(P\) people with mean time \(T\), its total time is \(PT\). The combined group contains \(20+P\) people and has mean \(56\), so
\[\frac{1080+PT}{20+P}=56.\]
Multiply by \(20+P\):
\[1080+PT=1120+56P.\]
Rearrange:
\[P(T-56)=40.\]
Therefore,
\[\boxed{P=\frac{40}{T-56}}.\]

The expression is
\[A=\frac{(x+y)^2zQ}{P}.\]
Increasing both \(x\) and \(y\) by \(50\%\) multiplies their sum by \(1.5\), so its square is multiplied by
\[(1.5)^2=2.25.\]
Decreasing \(z\) by \(20\%\) multiplies it by \(0.8\). Doubling \(P\), which is in the denominator, divides \(A\) by \(2\). Since \(Q\) is unchanged, the total multiplier is
\[\frac{2.25\times0.8}{2}=0.9.\]
The new value is \(90\%\) of the original, so \(A\) undergoes a \(\boxed{10\%\text{ decrease}}\).

Since \(AC\) is a diameter and \(B\) lies on the circle, \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\). Apply the Pythagorean theorem in triangle \(ABC\):
\[BC^2=AC^2-AB^2=20^2-12^2=256.\]
Thus \(BC=16\). Both \(\angle BAC\) and \(\angle BDC\) subtend chord \(BC\). Since the points \(A\) and \(D\) lie on the opposite arc from \(B\), these inscribed angles have the same sine. Therefore,
\[\sin\angle BDC=\sin\angle BAC=\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac{16}{20}=\boxed{0.8}.\]

Start with
\[t=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{2lR^2(W+w/3)}{n\pi r^4g}}.\]
Divide both sides by \(2\pi\) and square:
\[\frac{t^2}{4\pi^2}=\frac{2lR^2(W+w/3)}{n\pi r^4g}.\]
Multiply by \(n\pi r^4g\):
\[\frac{nr^4gt^2}{4\pi}=2lR^2\left(W+\frac w3\right).\]
Divide by \(2lR^2\):
\[W+\frac w3=\frac{nr^4gt^2}{8\pi lR^2}.\]
Finally, subtract \(\frac w3\):
\[\boxed{W=\frac{nr^4gt^2}{8\pi lR^2}-\frac w3}.\]

At \(9{:}45\), the minute hand points at the ninth hour marker, making an angle of
\[45\times6^\circ=270^\circ\]
from the twelve o'clock position. The hour hand starts at \(270^\circ\) at exactly nine o'clock and moves \(0.5^\circ\) per minute. After \(45\) minutes, it has moved
\[45\times0.5^\circ=22.5^\circ.\]
Therefore, the smaller angle between the two hands is \(\boxed{22.5^\circ}\).

Rearrange the given line to slope-intercept form:
\[4y+3x=8\implies y=-\frac34x+2.\]
Its slope is \(-\frac34\). A perpendicular line has slope \(\frac43\), the negative reciprocal. Using the point \((-6,2)\):
\[y-2=\frac43(x+6).\]
Multiply by \(3\):
\[3y-6=4x+24.\]
Rearrange into standard form:
\[\boxed{3y-4x=30}.\]

First calculate the square root:
\[\sqrt{1.6\times10^7}=\sqrt{16\times10^6}=4\times10^3.\]
Next, square the final factor:
\[(1.2\times10^3)^2=1.44\times10^6.\]
Substitute these results:
\[\frac{8\times10^{-5}}{4\times10^3}\times1.44\times10^6.\]
Simplify the fraction:
\[=2\times10^{-8}\times1.44\times10^6.\]
Multiply the coefficients and combine exponents:
\[\boxed{2.88\times10^{-2}}.\]

Evaluate each power in the numerator:
\[32^{1/5}=2,\qquad9^0=1.\]
The numerator is therefore \(2+1=3\). For the denominator, write \(81=3^4\):
\[81^{3/4}=(3^4)^{3/4}=3^3=27.\]
The fraction inside the parentheses is
\[\frac3{27}=\frac19.\]
A power of \(-1\) takes the reciprocal, so
\[\left(\frac19\right)^{-1}=\boxed{9}.\]

The surface area of a sphere of radius \(R\) is \(4\pi R^2\). Add the surface areas for the four given radii:
\[S=4\pi\left[\left(\frac r2\right)^2+r^2+(2r)^2+(3r)^2\right].\]
Square each radius and factor out \(r^2\):
\[S=4\pi r^2\left(\frac14+1+4+9\right).\]
The sum inside the parentheses is \(\frac{57}{4}\), so
\[S=4\pi r^2\cdot\frac{57}{4}=\boxed{57\pi r^2}.\]

A \(20\%\) reduction means the sale price is \(80\%\) of the original price. Let the original price be \(P\). Then
\[0.8P=32.\]
Divide by \(0.8\):
\[P=\frac{32}{0.8}=\boxed{40\text{ euros}}.\]

The first item exceeds the letter-size limits, so it must be sent as a parcel. Its weight is \(300\text{ g}\), consisting of the first \(30\text{ g}\) and nine additional \(30\text{ g}\) increments. Its cost is
\[1.22+9(0.17)=2.75.\]
The second item fits the letter dimensions and weighs \(110\text{ g}\). After the first \(30\text{ g}\), the remaining \(80\text{ g}\) requires three additional increments, because any part of \(30\text{ g}\) is charged as a full increment. Its cost is
\[0.44+3(0.17)=0.95.\]
The total postage is
\[2.75+0.95=\boxed{3.70\text{ dollars}}.\]

Sue and Freya start together, so the distance initially is zero. As Freya runs away, their separation increases; when Freya returns while Sue continues towards her, it decreases to zero. Their closing speed exceeds their separating speed, so the return segment is steeper. Graph B shows this pattern. Choose B.

Since the mean of \(a,b,c\) is \(8\), their sum is
\[a+b+c=3\times8=24.\]
The sum of the four new numbers is
\[(a+1)+(b+2)+(c+6)+3.\]
Group the original numbers and the additional constants:
\[=(a+b+c)+(1+2+6+3)=24+12=36.\]
Divide by the number of terms:
\[\frac{36}{4}=\boxed{9}.\]

Use the difference-of-squares identity
\[a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b).\]
For the first pair,
\[27^2-23^2=(27-23)(27+23)=4\times50=200.\]
For the second pair,
\[14^2-6^2=(14-6)(14+6)=8\times20=160.\]
Add the two results:
\[200+160=\boxed{360}.\]

Track vertex \(D\) through the first listed sequence. Since \(R\) advances one vertex and \(S\) reflects in the vertical axis, \(R,R,S,R,S,R\) sends \(D\to E\to A\to A\to B\to E\to A\). It ends at \(A\), not \(D\), so this sequence does not leave \(D\) in its original position. Choose A.

Let the shorter perpendicular side have length \(a\). The other perpendicular side is \(2a\). The area is
\[\frac12(a)(2a)=a^2.\]
Since the area is \(18\text{ cm}^2\),
\[a^2=18.\]
By the Pythagorean theorem, the hypotenuse \(h\) satisfies
\[h^2=a^2+(2a)^2=5a^2=5(18)=90.\]
Therefore,
\[h=\sqrt{90}=\boxed{3\sqrt{10}\text{ cm}}.\]

Factor the denominator of the first fraction:
\[x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1).\]
Rewrite the expression using a common denominator:
\[\frac2{(x-1)(x+1)}-\frac{x+1}{(x-1)(x+1)}.\]
Subtract the numerators:
\[=\frac{2-(x+1)}{(x-1)(x+1)}=\frac{1-x}{(x-1)(x+1)}.\]
Since \(1-x=-(x-1)\) and \(x\neq1\), cancel \(x-1\):
\[\boxed{-\frac1{x+1}}.\]

The line is
\[\frac x4+\frac y6=1.\]
To find its \(x\)-intercept, set \(y=0\):
\[\frac x4=1\implies x=4,\]
so \(A=(4,0)\). To find its \(y\)-intercept, set \(x=0\):
\[\frac y6=1\implies y=6,\]
so \(B=(0,6)\). The centre of a circle is the midpoint of its diameter. Therefore,
\[\left(\frac{4+0}{2},\frac{0+6}{2}\right)=\boxed{(2,3)}.\]

Multiply the given expressions:
\[xy=(3\times10^m)(5\times10^n).\]
Multiply the coefficients and add the powers of ten:
\[xy=15\times10^{m+n}.\]
Scientific notation requires a coefficient at least \(1\) and less than \(10\). Rewrite \(15=1.5\times10\):
\[xy=1.5\times10\times10^{m+n}.\]
Combine powers:
\[\boxed{xy=1.5\times10^{m+n+1}}.\]

A star is drawn from Box B in two mutually exclusive situations. First, a star is transferred from Box A, with probability \(\frac46\). Box B then has three stars among four shapes, so this case contributes
\[\frac46\times\frac34=\frac12.\]
Alternatively, a heart is transferred, with probability \(\frac26\). Box B then has two stars among four shapes, contributing
\[\frac26\times\frac24=\frac16.\]
Add the probabilities:
\[P(\text{star})=\frac12+\frac16=\boxed{\frac23}.\]

For \(0<x<1\), taking the reciprocal gives \(\frac1x>1\). Also, because \(0<x<1\), we have \(x<\sqrt{x}<1\), so
\[\frac1{\sqrt{x}}>1,\qquad\frac1x>\frac1{\sqrt{x}}.\]
The other expressions satisfy \(x^2<1\), \(\sqrt{x}<1\), and \(\frac1{1+x}<1\). Therefore, the largest expression is
\[\boxed{\frac1x}.\]

The difference being less than \(1\) means
\[|2\sqrt n-7|<1.\]
Rewrite as a double inequality:
\[-1<2\sqrt n-7<1.\]
Add \(7\) and divide by \(2\):
\[3<\sqrt n<4.\]
All terms are nonnegative, so squaring preserves the inequalities:
\[9<n<16.\]
The possible integers are \(10,11,12,13,14,15\), giving \(\boxed{6}\) values.

The midpoint of \(AB\) is \((\frac{2+6}{2},\frac{1+3}{2})=(4,2)\). The slope of \(AB\) is \((3-1)/(6-2)=1/2\), so its perpendicular bisector has slope \(-2\). Through \((4,2)\), its equation is \(y-2=-2(x-4)\), or \(y=10-2x\), option C.

If the square has side \(s\), the removed semicircle has radius \(s/2\). The remaining area is \(s^2-\frac12\pi(s/2)^2=s^2(1-\pi/8)=100\). Thus \(s^2=800/(8-\pi)\), giving \(s=20\sqrt{2/(8-\pi)}\) cm, option D.

Let \(L\) be the greater number and \(S\) the smaller number. Half their difference is \(2\):
\[\frac{L-S}{2}=2\implies L-S=4.\]
The second condition gives
\[L+2S=13.\]
From the first equation, \(L=S+4\). Substitute into the second:
\[S+4+2S=13.\]
Thus,
\[3S=9\implies\boxed{S=3}.\]

The brother receives \(\frac58\) of the \(5000\) stamps:
\[5000\times\frac58=3125.\]
He then divides his share between himself and two friends in the ratio \(3:1:1\), which contains \(5\) equal parts. Each friend receives one part, so
\[\frac{3125}{5}=\boxed{625\text{ stamps}}.\]

Start with
\[5n=\frac{m(ny-e^2)}p+n.\]
Subtract \(n\) from both sides:
\[4n=\frac{m(ny-e^2)}p.\]
Multiply by \(p\):
\[4np=m(ny-e^2)=mny-me^2.\]
Add \(me^2\) to both sides:
\[mny=4np+me^2.\]
Divide by \(mn\), assuming these factors are nonzero:
\[\boxed{y=\frac{4np+me^2}{mn}}.\]

The vectors \(p\) and \(q\) are nonzero and not parallel, so they are linearly independent. Therefore, their coefficients must match on both sides of
\[3p+(x-2)q=2yp-5q.\]
Compare the coefficients of \(p\):
\[3=2y\implies y=\frac32=1.5.\]
Compare the coefficients of \(q\):
\[x-2=-5\implies x=-3.\]
Hence,
\[\boxed{x=-3,\quad y=1.5}.\]

Each original tile has area
\[10\times10=100\text{ cm}^2.\]
The total covered area is
\[600\times100=60000\text{ cm}^2.\]
Each new tile has area
\[20\times20=400\text{ cm}^2.\]
Divide the total area by the area of one new tile:
\[\frac{60000}{400}=\boxed{150}.\]

A chained inequality requires both inequalities to hold:
\[x+2\le5+3x\quad\text{and}\quad5+3x\le2x+7.\]
For the first, subtract \(x\) and then \(5\):
\[-3\le2x\implies x\ge-\frac32.\]
For the second, subtract \(2x+5\):
\[x\le2.\]
Combining these conditions gives
\[\boxed{-1.5\le x\le2}.\]

Let the original total cost be \(C\). Under the initial ratio \(3:2\), the man pays
\[\frac35C.\]
When the cost doubles, the new total is \(2C\). The man must still pay \(\frac35C\), leaving the wife to pay
\[2C-\frac35C=\frac75C.\]
Their new contributions are therefore in the ratio
\[\frac35C:\frac75C=\boxed{3:7}.\]

Let Carol's share be \(x\). Brian receives three times as much, so his share is \(3x\). Ann receives twice Brian's share, giving \(6x\). Their total is
\[x+3x+6x=400.\]
Thus,
\[10x=400\implies x=40.\]
Brian receives
\[3x=3(40)=\boxed{120\text{ pounds}}.\]

Let the mass of raisins be \(r\). The sugar weighs \(1.5r\), and the flour weighs twice the sugar, or \(3r\). Their combined mass is \(550\text{ g}\):
\[r+1.5r+3r=550.\]
Combine like terms:
\[5.5r=550\implies r=100.\]
The flour weighs
\[3r=3(100)=\boxed{300\text{ g}}.\]

The original expression is
\[T=\frac{kx}{y}.\]
Increasing each variable by \(20\%\) multiplies it by \(1.2\). Therefore, the new value is
\[T'=\frac{(1.2k)(1.2x)}{1.2y}.\]
Cancel one factor of \(1.2\):
\[T'=1.2\frac{kx}{y}=1.2T.\]
The new value is \(120\%\) of the original, representing a \(\boxed{20\%\text{ increase}}\).

The runners move towards one another, so the distance between them decreases at the sum of their speeds:
\[4+6=10\text{ m/s}.\]
Convert the initial separation into metres:
\[1\text{ km}=1000\text{ m}.\]
Using \(t=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}\),
\[t=\frac{1000}{10}=\boxed{100\text{ s}}.\]

David's journey takes \(54\) minutes. Marian's journey takes \(80\%\) longer, so her travel time is
\[54(1+0.8)=97.2\text{ minutes}.\]
Convert this to hours:
\[\frac{97.2}{60}=1.62\text{ hours}.\]
Marian travels at \(70\text{ km/h}\), so her distance is
\[d=vt=70\times1.62=113.4\text{ km}.\]
Rounded to the nearest kilometre, this is \(\boxed{113\text{ km}}\).

Use the exponent rule \((a^m)^n=a^{mn}\):
\[(a^6)^{-2/3}=a^{6(-2/3)}=a^{-4}.\]
A negative exponent means the reciprocal:
\[a^{-4}=\frac1{a^4}.\]
Comparing this with \(\frac1{a^m}\) gives
\[\boxed{m=4}.\]

Let the first number be \(x\). The second is \(3x\), and the third is \(3x-7\). Their sum is \(28\), so
\[x+3x+(3x-7)=28.\]
Combine like terms:
\[7x-7=28\implies7x=35\implies x=5.\]
Therefore, the three numbers are
\[5,\quad3(5)=15,\quad15-7=8.\]
The result is \(\boxed{5,15,8}\).

Let Tina have \(x\) books. Stella has \(5x\). If Stella gives Tina \(16\) books, their new totals become \(5x-16\) and \(x+16\). They would then be equal, so
\[5x-16=x+16.\]
Rearrange:
\[4x=32\implies x=8.\]
Stella originally has
\[5x=5(8)=\boxed{40\text{ books}}.\]

Let the two journey distances be \(a\) and \(b\) metres. Using time = distance divided by speed, the two situations give
\[\frac a4+\frac b3=110,\]
\[\frac a3+\frac b4=100.\]
Multiply both equations by \(12\):
\[3a+4b=1320,\qquad4a+3b=1200.\]
Multiply the first by \(4\) and the second by \(3\):
\[12a+16b=5280,\qquad12a+9b=3600.\]
Subtract:
\[7b=1680\implies b=240.\]
Substitute into \(3a+4b=1320\):
\[3a+960=1320\implies a=120.\]
Thus the two distances are \(\boxed{120\text{ m and }240\text{ m}}\).

Let the cat's present age be \(c\) and the owner's present age be \(o\). In three years, the cat will be as old as the owner was four years ago:
\[c+3=o-4.\]
Thus, \(o=c+7\). Their present ages sum to \(13\):
\[c+o=13.\]
Substitute:
\[c+(c+7)=13\implies2c=6.\]
Therefore, the cat is \(\boxed{3\text{ years old}}\).

The events of selecting a white ball, a black ball, or a ball of another colour are mutually exclusive and together have total probability \(1\). Therefore,
\[P(\text{neither})=1-P(\text{white})-P(\text{black}).\]
Substitute the given probabilities:
\[P(\text{neither})=1-0.9-0.04=\boxed{0.06}.\]

Separate the fraction into two terms:
\[\frac{4\sqrt3+5\sqrt{60}}{2\sqrt3}=\frac{4\sqrt3}{2\sqrt3}+\frac{5\sqrt{60}}{2\sqrt3}.\]
Simplify the first term to \(2\). In the second, use \(\frac{\sqrt{60}}{\sqrt3}=\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt5\):
\[2+\frac52(2\sqrt5)=2+5\sqrt5.\]
Comparing with \(a+b\sqrt b\), we obtain
\[\boxed{a=2,\quad b=5}.\]

Let the original speed be \(v\text{ km/h}\). The original journey time is \(\frac{32}{v}\) hours, and the new time is \(\frac{32}{v+4}\) hours. The time saving is \(4\) hours:
\[\frac{32}{v}-\frac{32}{v+4}=4.\]
Combine the fractions:
\[\frac{128}{v(v+4)}=4.\]
Multiply and simplify:
\[v(v+4)=32\implies v^2+4v-32=0.\]
Factor:
\[(v+8)(v-4)=0.\]
Since speed must be positive, \(\boxed{v=4\text{ km/h}}\).

Distance is the area under the speed-time graph. The first triangular section has base \(2\) h and height \(30\) km/h, giving \(\frac12(2)(30)=30\) km. The second has base \(7-3=4\) h and height \(25\) km/h, giving \(50\) km. Total distance is \(30+50=80\) km, option C.

The equations are
\[4x-0.5y=12.5,\qquad3x+0.8y=8.2.\]
Multiply the first by \(8\) and the second by \(5\):
\[32x-4y=100,\qquad15x+4y=41.\]
Add the equations to eliminate \(y\):
\[47x=141\implies x=3.\]
Substitute into the first equation:
\[4(3)-0.5y=12.5.\]
Thus,
\[-0.5y=0.5\implies y=-1.\]
Therefore, \(\boxed{x=3,\ y=-1}\).

The cones are similar, so the ratio of corresponding lengths equals the ratio of their heights:
\[k=\frac{10}{6}=\frac53.\]
Volumes of similar solids scale by the cube of the linear scale factor. Thus,
\[\frac{V_B}{V_A}=\left(\frac53\right)^3=\frac{125}{27}.\]
Using \(V_A=189\text{ cm}^3\):
\[V_B=189\times\frac{125}{27}=7\times125.\]
Therefore,
\[\boxed{V_B=875\text{ cm}^3}.\]

The square has area \(12^2=144\text{ cm}^2\). The inscribed circle has diameter \(12\) cm and radius \(6\) cm, so its area is \(36\pi\text{ cm}^2\). The shaded area is \(144-36\pi=36(4-\pi)\text{ cm}^2\), option D.

Solve each inequality separately. For
\[3x-7<3-x,\]
add \(x+7\) to both sides:
\[4x<10\implies x<\frac52.\]
For the second inequality,
\[x-12\le3(x-3),\]
expand and rearrange:
\[x-12\le3x-9\implies-3\le2x,\]
so \(x\ge-\frac32\). Both conditions must hold, giving
\[\boxed{-1.5\le x<2.5}.\]

The diagram gives \(OA=5x,\ OC=4x,\ OB=5,\ OD=5+2x\). The ladder has the same length in both positions, so \(25x^2+25=16x^2+(5+2x)^2\). Expanding gives \(5x^2=20x\); with \(x>0\), \(x=4\). Its length is \(\sqrt{(5x)^2+5^2}=\sqrt{425}=5\sqrt{17}\approx20.6\) m, option B.

Start with
\[\frac{m(ny-e^2)}p+n=5n.\]
Subtract \(n\) from both sides:
\[\frac{m(ny-e^2)}p=4n.\]
Multiply by \(p\):
\[m(ny-e^2)=4np.\]
Expand:
\[mny-me^2=4np.\]
Add \(me^2\) and divide by \(mn\):
\[\boxed{y=\frac{4np+me^2}{mn}}.\]

The shares are divided in the ratio \(3:5:7\), so the total number of parts is
\[3+5+7=15.\]
Each part is worth
\[\frac{1050}{15}=70\text{ yuan}.\]
The difference between the largest and smallest shares is \(7-3=4\) parts. Therefore,
\[4\times70=\boxed{280\text{ yuan}}.\]

The volume of a cylinder is \(V=\pi r^2h\). Since its height is four times its radius, \(h=4r\). Substitute into the volume formula:
\[500\pi=\pi r^2(4r)=4\pi r^3.\]
Divide by \(4\pi\):
\[r^3=125.\]
Taking the cube root gives
\[\boxed{r=5\text{ cm}}.\]

The gradient of a line through \((x_1,y_1)\) and \((x_2,y_2)\) is
\[m=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}.\]
Using the points \((-3,7)\) and \((5,-8)\):
\[m=\frac{-8-7}{5-(-3)}.\]
Simplify the numerator and denominator:
\[m=\frac{-15}{8}=\boxed{-\frac{15}{8}}.\]

Both parts of the chained inequality must hold:
\[3y-4<12\quad\text{and}\quad12<4y-5.\]
From the first,
\[3y<16\implies y<\frac{16}{3}.\]
From the second,
\[17<4y\implies y>\frac{17}{4}.\]
Therefore,
\[\frac{17}{4}<y<\frac{16}{3}.\]
Since \(4.25<y<5.33\ldots\), the integer value satisfying both conditions is \(\boxed{y=5}\).

Expand the first product:
\[(x-y)(y+z)=xy+xz-y^2-yz.\]
Expand the second product:
\[(x+y)(y-z)=xy-xz+y^2-yz.\]
Subtract the entire second expression, changing the signs of all its terms:
\[xy+xz-y^2-yz-xy+xz-y^2+yz.\]
Cancel opposite terms and combine like terms:
\[\boxed{2xz-2y^2}.\]

Two counters have different colours if one is black and the other yellow. Since the draws are without replacement, there are two possible orders. Black then yellow has probability
\[\frac7{10}\times\frac39.\]
Yellow then black has probability
\[\frac3{10}\times\frac79.\]
Add the mutually exclusive cases:
\[P=\frac{21}{90}+\frac{21}{90}=\frac{42}{90}=\boxed{\frac7{15}}.\]

Since \(x\) is a prime number, it is a positive integer. From
\[x^2\le400,\]
take the positive square root to obtain
\[x\le20.\]
The largest prime number not exceeding \(20\) is \(19\), since \(20\) is composite. Check:
\[19^2=361\le400.\]
Therefore, \(\boxed{x=19}\).

A line parallel to the \(x\)-axis is horizontal, so every point on it has the same \(y\)-coordinate. The two given points are \((2m,n)\) and \((3,-4)\). Their \(y\)-coordinates must therefore satisfy
\[n=-4.\]
Hence,
\[\boxed{n=-4}.\]
Since \(AC\) is a diameter, \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\). Therefore \((x+35)+(2x-17)=90\), giving \(3x+18=90\). Hence \(x=24\), option C.

Travel time equals distance divided by speed. The outward journey takes
\[t_1=\frac{400}{x}\text{ hours}.\]
The return speed is \(x-60\), so the return journey takes
\[t_2=\frac{400}{x-60}\text{ hours}.\]
The return journey is \(20\) minutes longer. Convert this difference to hours:
\[20\text{ minutes}=\frac13\text{ hour}.\]
Therefore, return time minus outward time is
\[\boxed{\frac{400}{x-60}-\frac{400}{x}=\frac13}.\]

Substitute the given values:
\[\frac xy=\frac{2\times10^{10}}{16\times10^{11}}.\]
Divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents:
\[=\frac{2}{16}\times10^{10-11}=\frac18\times10^{-1}.\]
Convert the coefficient into standard scientific notation:
\[0.125\times10^{-1}=\boxed{1.25\times10^{-2}}.\]

Since \(ABCE\) is a parallelogram, \(AE=BC=11\) cm. Thus \(ED=15-11=4\) cm. From \([ECD]=\frac12(4)h=7\), the common height is \(h=3.5\) cm. The trapezium's area is \(\frac12(11+15)(3.5)=45.5\text{ cm}^2\), option C. In square metres this is \(0.00455\text{ m}^2\).

The radius \(OD\) is perpendicular to the tangent \(AD\). In triangle \(AOD\), \(\angle AOD=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ\). Since \(A,O,C\) are collinear, \(\angle DOC=150^\circ\). The isosceles triangle \(DOC\) has base angle \(\angle ODC=(180^\circ-150^\circ)/2=15^\circ\). Therefore \(\angle CDE=90^\circ-15^\circ=75^\circ\), option B.

Distance is the area under the speed-time graph. From \(10{:}00\) to \(10{:}15\), the triangular area is \(\frac12(\frac14)(70)=8.75\) km. The next \(15\) minutes at \(70\) km/h contribute \(17.5\) km. From \(10{:}30\) to \(11{:}00\), the trapezium contributes \(\frac{70+110}{2}(\frac12)=45\) km. Total distance is \(8.75+17.5+45=71.25\) km, option A.
The trapezium has parallel sides \(18x\) and \(10x\), separated by height \(3x\). Its area is \(\frac12(18x+10x)(3x)=\frac12(28x)(3x)=42x^2\text{ cm}^2\), option D.

All \(60\) pills belong to exactly one of the seven regions of a three-set Venn diagram. The three single-vitamin regions contain \(12+7+11=30\) pills, and \(6\) contain all three. Each of the three regions containing exactly two vitamins has \(x\) pills, so
\[30+6+3x=60.\]
Therefore,
\[3x=24\implies x=8.\]
Pills containing vitamin \(A\) include those with only \(A\), those with \(A\) and \(B\) only, those with \(A\) and \(C\) only, and those with all three:
\[12+8+8+6=\boxed{34}.\]

The box has square base \(x\) by \(x\) and height \(y\). Its volume gives \(x^2y=40\), so \(y=40/x^2\). The metal needed comprises the base and four side walls: \(S=x^2+4xy=x^2+4x(40/x^2)=x^2+160/x\), option A.
